Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module over $\mathbb Q(q)$ for a finite symmetrizable
Cartan datum such that

(a) $M$ is a weight module with $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}M_\mu<\infty$ for every
$\mu\in P$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]);

(b) the weight set $\mathrm{wt}(M)$ is bounded above: it is contained in a
finite union $\bigcup_{j=1}^s(\lambda_j-Q_+)$;

(c) $M$ is integrable, i.e. $E_i$ and $F_i$ act locally nilpotently for every
$i$.

Then $M$ is isomorphic to an algebraic direct sum of simple integrable highest
weight modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in P^+$
([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]);
concretely, every nonzero submodule of $M$ contains a maximal vector $v$ whose
cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$ for some
$\lambda\in P^+$, and $M$ is the direct sum of the submodules generated by the
vectors of any maximal independent family of simple submodules. AC is used
exactly to select a maximal independent family of simple submodules
simultaneously; restricted to any module generated by one finite-dimensional
$U^{\ge0}$-submodule the decomposition is obtained by a finite induction and is
choice-free. The finite-cone modules use the explicit label grading, and the
regularization supplier is used when the original pairing is not separating
([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]]).

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $G_\infty(b)$, $G_\lambda(\beta)$ be the lower global bases of $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. Then:

(i) $\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ is a based quotient over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if its crystal image $\pi_\lambda(b)\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is $0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise; consequently the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of exactly the killed lower global elements, the surviving elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, the module weight components are finite free over $A$, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the crystal compatibility of the completed grand loop, all for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label and auxiliary-realization convention;

(ii) more precisely, the integral kernel is
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-}\bigr)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}=\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}\bigr),$$
so the integral highest-module presentation uses all divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

For every dominant label weight $\lambda$, let $V_A=U_Av_\lambda=U_A^-v_\lambda$ be the integral highest lattice inside the simple integrable module $L(\lambda)$, over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Then each label-weight component of $V_A$ is finite free of rank $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}L(\lambda)_\mu$, not merely torsionfree, and $V_A$ spans the field module. For every characteristic-zero field $k$ specialized at $q=1$, the fibre has the same weight dimensions and is the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the explicitly regularized realization, transported back to the original label lattice; hence its character is the Weyl–Kac character, the finite Weyl character in finite type. The integral quotient $U_A^-/\sum_i\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}$ is $V_A(\lambda)$; its field extension is $L(\lambda)$ in every symmetrizable type.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: The Serre relation gives $XY=qYX$ and $YZ=qZY$. Mixed reordering gives $[F_i,Y]=E_jK_i^{-1}$ and $[Y,F_j]=K_jE_i$. For the first, expand $-H_iE_j+q^{-1}E_jH_i$ and move the torus to the right; its coefficient is $[-(q^{-1}K_i-qK_i^{-1})+q^{-1}(K_i-K_i^{-1})]/(q-q^{-1})=K_i^{-1}$. The second similarly has coefficient $H_j(qK_j)-q^{-1}H_j(K_j)=K_j$. Put $B=-qY$ and $C=-K_iF_i$. These identities give $CB-qBC=E_j$, $CE_j=q^{-1}E_jC$ and $E_jB=q^{-1}BE_j$. Thus $C^2B-(q+q^{-1})CBC+BC^2=q^{-1}[-CBC+qBC^2+E_jC]=0$, and the other Serre relation follows by using $E_jB=q^{-1}BE_j$. These are exactly the positive relations involving color $i$ after the proposed assignment. Applying $\psi$ gives the negative relations with their stated orders and coefficients.

Here are all other positive Serre checks. On a homogeneous element use $d(u)=E_iu-q^{\langle\mathrm{wt}(u),h_i\rangle}uE_i$, with $d(uv)=d(u)v+q^{\langle\mathrm{wt}(u),h_i\rangle}ud(v)$. For a neighbor, $d(E_j)=Y_{ij}$ and $d^2(E_j)=0$; for a nonneighbor $d(E_j)=0$. If commuting colors $j,k$ both neighbor $i$, apply $d^2$ to their commutator, obtaining $(q+q^{-1})[Y_{ij},Y_{ik}]=0$; if just one neighbors $i$, apply $d$ once. If $j,k$ are neighbors, the ADE diagram has no triangle, so at most one neighbors $i$. Apply $d^2$ to the Serre relation with that color repeated and $d$ to the other Serre relation. For example the three terms with repeated $j$ become respectively $(q+q^{-1})Y_{ij}^2E_k$, $(q+q^{-1})Y_{ij}E_kY_{ij}$ and $(q+q^{-1})E_kY_{ij}^2$. Their Serre combination vanishes. These cases exhaust the pairs away from $i$; applying $\psi$ gives all negative pairs.

For the mixed checks put $Z_{ik}=F_iF_k-q^{-1}F_kF_i$. For distinct neighbors $j,k$, expansion using their commuting opposite colors gives $[Y_{ij},Z_{ik}]=H_iE_jF_k-q^{-1}F_kH_iE_j-q^{-1}E_jH_iF_k+q^{-2}F_kE_jH_i$. Move the torus left. Since $E_jF_k$ has $i$-weight zero, the coefficient is $(1+q^{-2})H_i-q^{-1}(H_i(q^{-1}K_i)+H_i(qK_i))=0$. For $j=k$, step 1.1 instead gives $[Y_{ij},Z_{ij}]=-q^{-1}(H_jK_i^{-1}+K_jH_i)=-q^{-1}(K_iK_j-(K_iK_j)^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$, exactly the required mixed relation after multiplying $Y$ by $-q$. Pairs involving $i$ commute because $F_iZ_{ij}=qZ_{ij}F_i$ and $K_iZ_{ij}=q^{-1}Z_{ij}K_i$; the exchanged calculation handles the other half. The repeated $i$ mixed relation becomes $[-K_iF_i,-E_iK_i^{-1}]=-H_i$. Pairs with fewer neighboring colors commute immediately. Toral relations follow from the reflected weights. Thus the assignment preserves the full presentation.

We record an exact $A_2$ normal-order calculation. Write $x=E_i$, $z=E_j$, $y=xz-q^{-1}zx$ and $x^{(a)}=x^a/[a]!$, including $y^{(r)}=y^r/[r]!$ in the generic algebra. Then $$z^{(c)}x^{(a)}=\sum_{r=0}^{\min(a,c)}(-1)^rq^{(a-r)(c-r)+r}x^{(a-r)}y^{(r)}z^{(c-r)}.$$ Indeed $zx^{(p)}=q^px^{(p)}z-qx^{(p-1)}y$ and $zy^{(r)}=q^{-r}y^{(r)}z$. Writing $C_r(a,c)=(-1)^rq^{(a-r)(c-r)+r}$, multiplication by $z$ gives $[c+1]C_r(a,c+1)=q^{a-2r}[c-r+1]C_r(a,c)-q[r]C_{r-1}(a,c)$, where nonexistent terms are zero. Substitution reduces this to $[c+1]=q^{-r}[c-r+1]+q^{c-r+1}[r]$. This proves the formula by induction including both endpoints. In particular $x^{(a)}z^{(a+b)}x^{(b)}=z^{(b)}x^{(a+b)}z^{(a)}$: both expand as the sum over $0\le r\le b$ on $x^{(a+b-r)}y^{(r)}z^{(a+b-r)}$ with coefficient $(-1)^rq^{(a+b-r)(b-r)+r}\begin{bmatrix}a+b-r\\a\end{bmatrix}_q$.

Its inverse assignment is $E_i\mapsto-F_iK_i^{-1}$, $F_i\mapsto-K_iE_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{s_ih}$, and for a neighbor $E_j\mapsto E_iE_j-qE_jE_i$, $F_j\mapsto F_jF_i-q^{-1}F_iF_j$. The same checks with orders reversed prove it is a homomorphism. On a neighboring positive generator one composition is $CB-qBC=E_j$ from step 1.1. For the other put $C'=-F_iK_i^{-1}$, $B'=E_iE_j-qE_jE_i$; mixed reordering gives $[F_i,B']=E_jK_i$, hence $C'B'=q^{-1}B'C'-q^{-1}E_j$ and $B'C'-qC'B'=E_j$. The negative checks apply $\psi$, and the $i$ and toral compositions cancel directly. Both compositions are the identity on all generators.

On a finite generic rank-one string of highest label $m$ define $Q_i(F_i^{(r)}u)=(-1)^rq^{r(m-r+1)}F_i^{(m-r)}u$. It is invertible and conjugates its one-color action by $S_i$. For a neighbor, $E_j$ commutes $F_i$, and $E_i^2E_ju=0$. By [F2], $E_ju$ splits into a highest vector $a$ of label $m-1$ and $F_ib$, with $b$ highest of label $m+1$. On the $a$ component, with $s=m-r$, the coefficient of $YF_i^{(s)}u$ is $[m-s]-q^{-1}[m-s+1]=-q^{-m+s-1}$. Multiplication by $-q$ gives $q^{-r}$, exactly the ratio between the two $Q_i$ string coefficients. On the $F_ib$ component it is $[m-s+1]([s+1]-q^{-1}[s])=[r+1]q^{m-r}$; multiplication by $-q$ and the original string coefficient gives $[r+1](-1)^{r+1}q^{(r+1)(m-r+1)}$, again the coefficient of $Q_iE_j$. Therefore $Q_iE_j=S_i(E_j)Q_i$.

From step 2.3 and quantum Pascal induction one gets $y^{(n)}=\sum_{r+s=n}(-1)^rq^{-r}x^{(s)}z^{(n)}x^{(r)}$. Multiplying by $(-q)^n$ and exchanging $r,s$ gives the stated divided formula for $S_i(E_j^{(n)})$; applying $\psi$ gives the negative formula. On color $i$ ordinary multiplication gives $S_i(E_i^{(n)})=(-1)^nq^{n(n-1)}K_i^nF_i^{(n)}$ and $S_i(F_i^{(n)})=(-1)^nq^{-n(n-1)}E_i^{(n)}K_i^{-n}$. Inverses have the same integral formulas with order reversed. Thus they preserve the subalgebra $B$ generated by divided $E,F$ powers and $K_h$.

For the negative generator start at a lowest vector $l$ of label $-m$. Then $Q_i(E_i^{(r)}l)=d_r(m)E_i^{(m-r)}l$, where $d_r(m)=(-1)^{m-r}q^{(m-r)(r+1)}$. Now $F_jl$ splits into a lowest $a$ of label $-(m-1)$ and $E_ib$, with $b$ lowest of label $-(m+1)$. The coefficient of $S_i(F_j)E_i^{(s)}l$ on the first is $-q^{-m+s-1}=-q^{-r-1}$, and $d_r(m)(-q^{-r-1})=d_r(m-1)$. On the second it is $[r+1]q^{m-r}$, and $d_r(m)[r+1]q^{m-r}=[r+1]d_{r+1}(m+1)$. Thus $Q_iF_j=S_i(F_j)Q_i$. Nonneighbors commute with the full rank-one action and hence with its explicit $Q_i$. We have proved $Q_iu=S_i(u)Q_i$ on every generator.

In $A_2$ the identity $CB-qBC=E_j$ also gives $S_iS_j(E_i)=E_j$ and its exchanged version. Applying $\psi$ gives the negative identities. Thus the two three-term products of the $S$ maps agree on the rank-two algebra; both send $E_i$ to $-K_jF_j$ and $E_j$ to $-K_iF_i$. On its highest module of label $(a,b)$ the corresponding $Q$ products send the highest vector to $F_i^{(b)}F_j^{(a+b)}F_i^{(a)}u$ and $F_j^{(a)}F_i^{(a+b)}F_j^{(b)}u$, equal by step 2.3. Each intermediate vector is highest for the next color: for example $E_iF_j^{(a+b)}F_i^{(a)}u=F_j^{(a+b)}F_i^{(a-1)}u=0$, since the latter intermediate highest label for color $j$ is $a+b-1$. Their conjugations agree, so the $Q$ products agree on the entire cyclic module. By [F2] this holds on every finite module after rank-two restriction. For nonneighbors, restrictions are direct sums of tensor products of two independent strings, on which the two $Q$ operators commute.

Finite generic integrable modules separate the algebra. For a nonzero element in triangular form choose an integral toral label $\xi$ at which one nonzero Laurent coefficient stays nonzero; a Laurent polynomial cannot vanish on every grid $(q^{n_1},\ldots,q^{n_r})$. On a lowest-highest tensor of labels $-a,b$, $b-a=\xi$, an ordered positive-negative half product has the corresponding pure tensor as leading term, with a Laurent unit coefficient and corrections of smaller total half degree, by the triangular coproduct. Choose $a,b$ large enough that the exact highest/lowest half kernels in [F3], generated by divided singular powers beyond their limits, have degrees greater than every half degree in this finite expression. The leading term survives, giving a finite module on which the element acts nontrivially. Therefore the operator braid relations from step 6.1, together with the conjugations in steps 4.1–2.4 and invertibility of $Q_i$, imply the algebra braid relations on every generator, including colors outside the rank-two pair.

This $B$ is the full form. Induct on $t$ in $E_i^{(t)}F_i^{(t)}=\sum_{r=0}^tF_i^{(t-r)}T_{i,2r-2t,r}E_i^{(t-r)}$. The $r=t$ term is $T_{i,0,t}$ and the others have smaller lower index. All shifts are supplied by the integral Vandermonde identity $T_{i,c,t}=\sum_{a+b=t}q^{-bc}\begin{bmatrix}c\\a\end{bmatrix}_qK_i^aT_{i,0,b}$, valid for every integer $c$ with Laurent-polynomial Gaussians, by [F1]. Hence every toral binomial belongs to $B$. Preservation of $B$ really is preservation of $U_A$, so specialization induces inverse automorphisms of the actual algebra. Their generator formulas also preserve the ordinary form and its inverse map over the stated localization. This proves every assertion, with exactly the inherited Choice in [F4].

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), put
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), let
$L:=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb Z(d_ih_i)\subseteq P^{\vee}$, and let $U_A^0$ be the
$A$-subalgebra of $U_q^0$ generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the toral quantum
binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]).

(a) **One simple torus.** Fix $i\in I$ and write $z:=q_i$, $K:=K_i$,
$T_t:=T_{i,0,t}$ for $t\ge0$. Then for all $r,s\ge0$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and
$t\ge1$,
$$T_rT_s=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(r,s)}z^{rs}K^{-j}\binom{r+s-j}{r}_z\binom{r}{j}_zT_{r+s-j},\qquad T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^{-1}z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1},$$
where $\binom{m}{r}_z$ is the Gaussian binomial of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]; all
coefficients lie in $A$. Moreover the $A$-subalgebra of $U_q^0$ generated by
$K^{\pm1}$ and all $T_{c,t}$ equals the $A$-span of
$\{K^{\delta}T_t:\delta\in\{0,1\},\,t\ge0\}$, and that set is an $A$-basis.

(b) **Full torus.** Fix a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $P^{\vee}$, let $J$ be the
finite set of coordinates occurring in the finitely many vectors $d_ih_i$, and
let $D:=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathbb Z e_j$ be the corresponding coordinate direct
summand. For every coset of $L$ in $P^{\vee}$ choose the representative $c$
whose $D$-component has minimal sum of coordinate absolute values, ties broken
lexicographically, and whose complementary component is the coset's common
complementary component. Then
$$U_A^0=\bigoplus_{c}K_c\cdot A\text{-span}\Bigl\{\prod_{i\in I}K_i^{\delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}:\delta_i\in\{0,1\},\,t_i\ge0\Bigr\},$$
the sum over the chosen representatives, so the displayed elements form an
$A$-basis of $U_A^0$.

Both statements are proved directly on the unmodified generators over the
non-PID ring $A$: no integral PBW or canonical-basis input, no inference from
torsion-freeness to freeness, and no modified-${}_A\dot U$ result is used.

Let $z$ be a primitive root of odd order $\ell>1$. Write $N=\ell N_1+N_0$ for $N\in\mathbb Z$ and $r=\ell r_1+r_0$ for $r\ge0$, with $0\le N_0,r_0<\ell$. The symmetric quantum binomial, interpreted by its Laurent-polynomial product for negative upper index, satisfies
$$\begin{bmatrix}N\\r\end{bmatrix}_z=\binom{N_1}{r_1}\begin{bmatrix}N_0\\r_0\end{bmatrix}_z.$$
For a specialized family $X^{(n)}$ with the divided-power multiplication of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]],
$$X^{(a\ell+r)}=\frac{(X^{(\ell)})^aX^r}{a![r]_z!}\qquad(a\ge0,\ 0\le r<\ell).$$
In particular the family is generated by $X$ and $X^{(\ell)}$; modulo the ideal generated by $X$, a divided power vanishes unless its index is divisible by $\ell$, and $X^{(a\ell)}=(X^{(\ell)})^a/a!$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

derivations.claim: Fix one color. Modulo $K=1$, the first recurrence of [F1] gives $T_{a\ell+1}=0$: its right numerator is zero and its left scalar $z-z^{-1}$ is nonzero. Successively for $1<r<\ell$, the scalar $z^r-z^{-r}$ is nonzero and the preceding term vanishes, so $T_{a\ell+r}=0$. In the product formula of [F1] with $r=\ell$, $s=a\ell$, Lucas makes all terms vanish except $j=0$ and $j=\ell$; these have coefficients $a+1$ and $a$, respectively. Thus $H T_{a\ell}=(a+1)T_{(a+1)\ell}+aT_{a\ell}$, where $H=T_\ell$. Induction from $T_0=1$ gives $T_{a\ell}=\binom Ha$. The toral spanning statement in [F1] now shows that the full quotient by all $K_h-1$ is spanned by polynomials in the $H_i$.

For each $\mu\in P$, evaluate the integral torus at $K_h=q^{\langle\ell\mu,h\rangle}$ and then specialize $q=\zeta$. These are well-defined integral evaluations, since a toral binomial evaluates to the Laurent-integral quantum binomial with upper index $\langle\ell\mu,h_i\rangle+c$, including negative indices by [F2]. They annihilate every $K_h-1$ and send $H_i$ to $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$. The coordinate image of $P$ is a finite-index subgroup of $\mathbb Z^I$, since $P$ has finite index in the full weight lattice; hence it contains $N\mathbb Z^I$ for some positive integer $N$. A polynomial vanishing on this grid is zero: regard it as a polynomial in one variable with infinitely many grid values, then apply the same argument to each coefficient in the other finitely many variables. There is consequently no polynomial relation among the $H_i$ in the quotient. This proves its exact polynomial-algebra description.

Every $T_{i,c,t}$ is already a polynomial in $H_i$ in the quotient by step 1.1 and the toral shift spanning. Its evaluation at $\mu$ in step 2.1 is $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}\ell\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c\\t\end{smallmatrix}\right]_{z_i}=\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c_1}{t_1}\left[\begin{smallmatrix}c_0\\t_0\end{smallmatrix}\right]_{z_i}$ by [F2]. Polynomial separation from step 2.1 gives the formula in the statement, including negative $c$. In particular $T_{i,-\ell a_{ij},\ell}=H_i-a_{ij}$ in this quotient.

Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. For a finite simply-laced root datum with full weight lattice and $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, the generic algebra has automorphisms $S_i$ with
$$S_i(K_h)=K_{s_i h},\qquad S_i(E_i)=-K_iF_i,\qquad S_i(F_i)=-E_iK_i^{-1}.$$
They fix $E_j,F_j$ for $a_{ij}=0$, while for $a_{ij}=-1$,
$$S_i(E_j)=E_jE_i-qE_iE_j,\qquad S_i(F_j)=F_iF_j-q^{-1}F_jF_i.$$
They satisfy $S_iS_j=S_jS_i$ for nonneighbors and $S_iS_jS_i=S_jS_iS_j$ for neighbors. They and their inverses preserve the entire divided-power form $U_A$, including its toral binomials, and the ordinary-generator form over $A[(q-q^{-1})^{-1}]$. They consequently specialize to inverse automorphisms whenever the indicated denominators are invertible. For neighbors,
$$S_i(E_j^{(n)})=\sum_{r+s=n}(-1)^rq^rE_i^{(r)}E_j^{(n)}E_i^{(s)},\qquad S_i(F_j^{(n)})=\sum_{r+s=n}(-1)^rq^{-r}F_i^{(s)}F_j^{(n)}F_i^{(r)}.$$
No root-of-unity PBW or small-quantum-group theorem is assumed in this assertion.

Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, $K=\mathbb C((\hbar))$, $q=e^\hbar$, and $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$ for a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum. Let $H^+=U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\langle V\rangle$ and the shuffle product be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], and put $H^-=T(V^*)/J_-$ using [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]]. Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the formal embedding theorem. For an indeterminate $z$, let $H_z^\pm$ be the algebras over $\mathbb C(z)$ presented by the separate symmetric quantum Serre relations, with parameters $z_i=z^{d_i}$.

(i) Each $H^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is finite free over $R$, and
$$\operatorname{rank}_R H^\pm[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak n^\pm)[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(z)}H_z^\pm[\pm\alpha].$$
Every family of homogeneous lifts of a basis of the classical component is an $R$-basis. Likewise, homogeneous word expressions with coefficients rational in $z$, regular at $z=1$, which reduce to a classical component basis form a basis of the corresponding generic component. In particular, for a supplied ordered homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak n^\pm$, ordered monomials in any such regular lifts form a generic PBW basis.

(ii) Both formal halves are graded braided Hopf algebras. Their generators are primitive, their counits kill positive height, and their tensor squares use
$$ (u\otimes v)(u'\otimes v')=q^{-\langle\deg u',\deg v\rangle}uu'\otimes vv',\qquad \langle\epsilon_i,\epsilon_j\rangle=d_i a_{ij},$$
with negative degrees for $H^-$. The word pairing restricts and descends to a nondegenerate $K$-valued pairing $H^+\times H^-$ with $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}/(\hbar d_i)$ and $\langle1,1\rangle=1$. It is zero on unequal opposite degrees and satisfies the braided Hopf adjunctions
$$\langle x,yy'\rangle=\sum\langle x_{(1)},y\rangle\langle x_{(2)},y'\rangle,\qquad\langle xx',y\rangle=\sum\langle x,y_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',y_{(2)}\rangle.$$
The generic halves have the same braided Hopf structures and a nondegenerate $\mathbb C(z)$-valued pairing normalized by $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle_z=\delta_{ij}/(z_i-z_i^{-1})$. Thus opposite graded components are dual. All generic assertions also hold for the corresponding $\mathbb Q(z)$-presentations and their rational pairing, with the PBW lift clause using bases of the rational classical Serre form.

Let $R=(X,\Phi,X^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$ be a reduced root datum ([[def-abstract-root-datum-and-its-weyl-group]]). Then: (a) $W(R)$ is finite and generated by the reflections $s_\alpha$, $\alpha\in\Phi$; for a base $\Delta\subseteq\Phi$ it is generated by the simple reflections $s_\alpha$, $\alpha\in\Delta$; (b) the correspondences between bases, positive systems and Weyl chambers are bijective, and $W(R)$ acts simply transitively on the set of Weyl chambers, equivalently on the set of bases; (c) for a chosen positive system $\Phi^+$ there is a unique longest element $w_0\in W(R)$ with $w_0(\Phi^+)=-\Phi^+$, and for every $w\in W(R)$ the integer $n(w)=|\Phi^+\cap w(\Phi^-)|$ equals the length of $w$ with respect to the simple reflections, with $n(w^{-1})=n(w)$ and $n(w_0w)=|\Phi^+|-n(w)$; (d) $\Phi$ spans $V=X\otimes\mathbb Q$ iff the root datum is semisimple, and then $\Phi$ is a reduced root system in $V$ in the Euclidean sense.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix; let $W$ and $\ell$ be the presented group and its length and let $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ be the geometric representation, as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], with reflection set $T$ and sign-change sets $\Phi(w)$ as in that lemma. Parts (1) and (2) hold for every finite $S$, including the empty and singleton cases; a distinct pair is required only for part (3).

1. **Braid moves.** Call two words in $S$ *braid-equivalent* when one is obtained from the other by finitely many replacements of an alternating subword $s\,t\,s\,t\cdots$ of length $m(s,t)<\infty$ by the alternating word $t\,s\,t\,s\cdots$ of the same length. Then any two reduced expressions of the same element $w\in W$ are braid-equivalent.
2. **M-reducedness.** A word is reduced if and only if no sequence of braid moves followed by cancellation of a consecutive equal pair can shorten it (M-reduced in the sense of [Davis, Definition 3.4.1]).
3. **Singleton detection in dihedral subgroups.** Fix distinct $s,t\in S$ and put $m:=m(s,t)$. The subgroup $\langle s,t\rangle\le W$ is dihedral of order $2m$ when $m<\infty$ and infinite dihedral when $m=\infty$; every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ acts on the quotient $E/\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ as the identity, while for every $u\in S\setminus\{s,t\}$ one has $\sigma_u(\alpha_u)-\alpha_u=-2\alpha_u\notin\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ (no induced quotient map for $\sigma_u$ is assumed). Consequently
$$S\cap\langle s,t\rangle=\{s,t\},$$
and every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ has a reduced expression with all letters in $\{s,t\}$ (so the alternating words of length $q\le m$, and any $q$ when $m=\infty$, are reduced in $W$).

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

Let $S$ be a finite set, $m$ a Coxeter matrix, $W$ the presented group with length $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), $V=\mathbb R^S$ with Coxeter form $B$, canonical reflection homomorphism $\rho$, root system $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$ and reflection set $T=\{wsw^{-1}:w\in W,\ s\in S\}$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]], [[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]]); every root has $B$-norm one.

**(1) The root-reflection dictionary.** For $\alpha\in\Phi$ choose $w\in W$, $s\in S$ with $\alpha=\rho(w)e_s$ and put $t_\alpha:=wsw^{-1}\in T$. Then:
(i) $t_\alpha$ is independent of the chosen representation of $\alpha$;
(ii) $\rho(t_\alpha)=r_\alpha$, the reflection with normal $\alpha$; and $t_{\rho(w)\alpha}=w\,t_\alpha\,w^{-1}$ for all $w\in W$, $\alpha\in\Phi$;
(iii) $t_{-\alpha}=t_\alpha$, and for $\alpha,\beta\in\Phi$ one has $t_\alpha=t_\beta$ if and only if $\alpha=\pm\beta$;
(iv) the induced map $\{\pm\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi\}\to T$ is a bijection; so is the map $\Phi_+\to T$, $\alpha\mapsto t_\alpha$.

**(2) Inversion formula.** For every $w\in W$ one has $|N(w)|=\ell(w)$ (with $N$ as in [[def-cg-geometric-inversion-set]]); and for every reduced expression $w=s_1\cdots s_n$,
$$N(w)=\bigl\{\rho(s_{i+1}\cdots s_n)^{-1}e_{s_i}:1\le i\le n\bigr\},\qquad N(w^{-1})=\bigl\{\rho(s_1\cdots s_{i-1})e_{s_i}:1\le i\le n\bigr\},$$
the displayed elements being pairwise distinct positive roots.

**(3) Strong exchange.** Let $w\in W$ and $t\in T$ satisfy $\ell(tw)<\ell(w)$, and let $w=s_1\cdots s_n$ be a reduced expression. Then there is a unique $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ with
$$tw=s_1\cdots\widehat{s_i}\cdots s_n,\qquad t=r_i:=s_1\cdots s_{i-1}s_is_{i-1}\cdots s_1;$$
moreover, if $\alpha\in\Phi_+$ is the positive root with $t=t_\alpha$, then $\alpha\in N(w^{-1})$ and $\alpha=\rho(s_1\cdots s_{i-1})e_{s_i}$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: If $\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1$, then $S_w(E_i)$ is positive. Prove this by induction on $\ell(w)$. Choose a right descent $j$ of a nonidentity $w$; necessarily $j\ne i$. Write $w=w'v$ with $w'$ the minimal right coset representative for $\{i,j\}$ and $v$ in that rank-two parabolic. Both $i,j$ are ascents of $w'$. Since $i$ is an ascent and $j$ a descent of $v$, its alternating reduced word has length at most $m_{ij}-1$. The rank-two calculations in [F1] therefore make $S_v(E_i)$ either a simple generator or one of the two neighboring positive polynomials $E_jE_i-qE_iE_j$ and $E_iE_j-qE_jE_i$. Induction makes both $S_{w'}(E_i),S_{w'}(E_j)$ positive, hence also $S_w(E_i)$. Its divided powers belong to $U_A$ by [F1], so [F2] puts them in $U_A^+$. Apply this to every prefix in the chosen reduced word.

Let $M_{\mathbf i}$ be the $A$-span of the ordered divided root monomials for the word $\mathbf i$. A braid move changes only its local root block; later factors agree by the braid relation. For commuting colors the block spans agree by commutation. For $A_2$ put $x=E_i$, $z=E_j$, $y=xz-q^{-1}zx$. Up to Laurent units its three root factors are $x,y,z$. The exact identity from [F1] is $$z^{(c)}x^{(a)}=\sum_{r=0}^{\min(a,c)}(-1)^rq^{(a-r)(c-r)+r}x^{(a-r)}y^{(r)}z^{(c-r)}.$$ It shows that the span of $x^{(a)}y^{(b)}z^{(c)}$ contains $1$ and is stable under every left divided power of $x$ and $z$: use $zy=q^{-1}yz$ and divided multiplication after the displayed formula. Thus it is the entire divided rank-two half. The reversed block has the same property, so both integral block spans agree. Applying their common preceding $S$ prefix preserves equality. By [F4] the space $M_{\mathbf i}$ is independent of the reduced word.

Every simple color $i$ starts some reduced word for $w_0$. In that word $E_i^{(r)}$ multiplies the first root factor by the Gaussian coefficient $\begin{bmatrix}r+a_1\\r\end{bmatrix}_q\in A$. Hence the common space from step 2.1 is stable under every divided simple generator. It contains $1$ and lies in $U_A^+$ by step 1.1, so it equals $U_A^+$. In any fixed weight $\nu$, the ordered root monomials number the Kostant partitions of $\nu$, exactly the generic dimension in [F3]. Since they span, they are linearly independent over the generic field and therefore over $A$. They form an integral basis, not just a torsion-free spanning set. The half exchange gives the negative result. Base change of these actual free bases retains the bases at every scalar parameter.

Repeat the block-span argument for ordinary powers over $A[(q-q^{-1})^{-1}]$. In $A_2$ the relations $zx=qxz-qy$, $xy=qyx$ and $yz=qzy$ reorder ordinary words with coefficients in this ring and no divided factorial. Thus the ordinary block span is the entire ordinary rank-two algebra, and the common-span argument applies. A positive root vector belongs to the ordinary half: it lies in the ordinary full form by [F1], and projecting an ordinary mixed normal-order expansion onto negative degree zero and toral exponent zero maps each normal-ordered word into the ordinary positive half and fixes a pure positive element. Mixed reordering uses only the inverted $q-q^{-1}$. This justifies the positivity-intersection step for the ordinary form without assuming its integral PBW theorem. Its common root-monomial span is stable under all ordinary $E_i$, by choosing a word starting $i$, and hence equals its ordinary half. Exchanging halves completes the ordinary assertion.

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

derivations.claim: Fix one root color, and first work in a single $P/\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ coset. Take a finite-dimensional simple graded module for the rank-one algebra, and choose a nonzero vector $v$ at its highest integer coroot label $n$. It is killed by every positive divided power. Reordering shows that the cyclic module is spanned by the distinct weight vectors $F^{(r)}v$, $r\ge0$, and simplicity makes this the whole module. If $n=-b<0$, put $r=2\ell k$. The negative-binomial identity gives $\begin{bmatrix}-b\\r\end{bmatrix}_\zeta=(-1)^r\begin{bmatrix}b+r-1\\r\end{bmatrix}_\zeta$. To see this is nonzero for arbitrarily large $k$, write $b-1=a\ell+s$, $0\le s<\ell$, and use $\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+\zeta^{N-1-2j}z)=\sum_j\begin{bmatrix}N\\j\end{bmatrix}_\zeta z^j$ with $N=b+r-1$. Every block of length $\ell$ equals $1+\zeta^{\ell(N-1)}z^\ell$, because $\zeta^{-2}$ has odd order $\ell$; the residual block has degree $s<\ell$. The coefficient of $z^{2\ell k}$ is therefore $\binom{a+2k}{2k}$: the sign from $\zeta^{\ell(N-1)}=\pm1$ is raised to the even power $2k$. It is nonzero. But finite support makes $F^{(r)}v=0$ for large $r$, contradicting $E^{(r)}F^{(r)}v=\begin{bmatrix}n\\r\end{bmatrix}_\zeta v$. Hence $n\ge0$.

For this simple cyclic module the span of $F^{(r)}v$, $r>n$, is stable. Positive divided powers landing at index $r-s\le n$ have coefficient $\begin{bmatrix}n-r+s\\s\end{bmatrix}_\zeta=0$, since the upper index is then a nonnegative integer smaller than $s$; all other terms remain in that span. Negative divided powers increase the index and toral operators act diagonally. This is a proper submodule, as it avoids the top weight, so it is zero. The module is thus a quotient of the specialized free rank-one string $W(n)$ with basis $u_0,\ldots,u_n$ and the actions in [F1]. On $W(n)$ the diagonal bilinear form $(u_r,u_r)=\begin{bmatrix}n\\r\end{bmatrix}_\zeta$, $(u_r,u_s)=0$ for $r\ne s$, is contravariant for $E^{(a)}\leftrightarrow F^{(a)}$ and fixes the torus. Indeed the required identity is $\begin{bmatrix}n\\r\end{bmatrix}_q\begin{bmatrix}r\\a\end{bmatrix}_q=\begin{bmatrix}n\\r-a\end{bmatrix}_q\begin{bmatrix}n-r+a\\a\end{bmatrix}_q$, valid as a Laurent-polynomial identity before specialization. Its radical is consequently stable. Every surviving weight line of the quotient by this radical can be raised to $u_0$ using $E^{(r)}$, since its coefficient is nonzero; the quotient is simple. Every proper graded submodule of $W(n)$ lies in the radical, since it cannot contain $u_0$ and the same raising test applies. Therefore the original simple module is this quotient. Its surviving indices are exactly those $r$ with $\begin{bmatrix}n\\r\end{bmatrix}_\zeta\ne0$, a set invariant under $r\mapsto n-r$ by Gaussian symmetry. Its character is reflected about coroot label zero.

Every finite-dimensional graded rank-one module has a composition series in the graded module category: choose proper graded submodules of largest dimension and continue, so the process terminates. Its simple quotients have the symmetric characters proved in steps 1.1 and 2.1; character additivity proves symmetry for the original module. Coset by coset, the reflection sends $\mu$ to $\mu-\langle\mu,h_i\rangle\alpha_i$, so this is precisely $s_i$-invariance of $\operatorname{ch}M$. Applying this for each color gives Weyl invariance.

Now let $v$ be any nonzero rank-one highest vector, without simplicity. Its finite cyclic module is spanned by $F^{(r)}v$ and has support at $n-2r$, $r\ge0$. By step 3.1 this support is invariant under negation, forcing $n\ge0$. Its span of indices $r>n$ is a submodule by the calculation in step 2.1, and all its coroot labels are strictly negative. Applying step 3.1 to this finite submodule forces it to be zero. Thus every higher divided power $F^{(r)}v$ with $r>n$ vanishes. This proves the stated highest-vector assertion for every color.

citations.quote: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. In finite simply-laced type choose a reduced word $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_N}$ and set $\beta_t=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{t-1}}\alpha_{i_t}$ and $X_{\beta_t}=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_{t-1}}(E_{i_t})$, using [[lem-simply-laced-quantum-braid-symmetries-preserve-the-integral-form]]. Then every $X_{\beta_t}$ is positive and $X_{\beta_t}^{(r)}=X_{\beta_t}^r/[r]_q!$ lies in the positive divided half. The ordered monomials $X_{\beta_1}^{(a_1)}\cdots X_{\beta_N}^{(a_N)}$, $a_t\ge0$, are an actual $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of that half. Exchanging the positive and negative halves gives the negative root basis. Both bases remain bases after every scalar specialization. Over $A[(q-q^{-1})^{-1}]$, the corresponding ordinary root monomials span the ordinary-generator halves. The assertion includes every reduced convex word, rather than one unnamed PBW ordering.

Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. For a finite simply-laced root datum with full weight lattice and $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, the generic algebra has automorphisms $S_i$ with
$$S_i(K_h)=K_{s_i h},\qquad S_i(E_i)=-K_iF_i,\qquad S_i(F_i)=-E_iK_i^{-1}.$$
They fix $E_j,F_j$ for $a_{ij}=0$, while for $a_{ij}=-1$,
$$S_i(E_j)=E_jE_i-qE_iE_j,\qquad S_i(F_j)=F_iF_j-q^{-1}F_jF_i.$$
They satisfy $S_iS_j=S_jS_i$ for nonneighbors and $S_iS_jS_i=S_jS_iS_j$ for neighbors. They and their inverses preserve the entire divided-power form $U_A$, including its toral binomials, and the ordinary-generator form over $A[(q-q^{-1})^{-1}]$. They consequently specialize to inverse automorphisms whenever the indicated denominators are invertible. For neighbors,
$$S_i(E_j^{(n)})=\sum_{r+s=n}(-1)^rq^rE_i^{(r)}E_j^{(n)}E_i^{(s)},\qquad S_i(F_j^{(n)})=\sum_{r+s=n}(-1)^rq^{-r}F_i^{(s)}F_j^{(n)}F_i^{(r)}.$$
No root-of-unity PBW or small-quantum-group theorem is assumed in this assertion.

Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the integral triangular-decomposition supplier. The full form $U_A$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], including every $T_{i,c,t}$, is stable under the library coproduct, counit, antipode and inverse antipode. Consequently every scalar specialization, including $U^L_\zeta$, is a Hopf algebra with bijective antipode. In the following formulas $a,b,r,t\ge0$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, and $q=q_i$, $K=K_i$ when the color is suppressed:

$$\Delta E_i^{(r)}=\sum_{a+b=r}q_i^{ab}E_i^{(a)}\otimes K_i^{-a}E_i^{(b)},\qquad \Delta F_i^{(r)}=\sum_{a+b=r}q_i^{-ab}F_i^{(a)}K_i^b\otimes F_i^{(b)}.$$

$$\Delta T_{i,c,t}=\sum_{a+b=t}q_i^{-bc}T_{i,c,a}K_i^{-b}\otimes K_i^aT_{i,0,b}.$$

$$S(E_i^{(r)})=(-1)^rq_i^{r(r-1)}E_i^{(r)}K_i^r,\qquad S(F_i^{(r)})=(-1)^rq_i^{-r(r-1)}K_i^{-r}F_i^{(r)}.$$

$$S(T_{i,c,t})=(-1)^tT_{i,t-c-1,t},\qquad \varepsilon(T_{i,c,t})=\begin{bmatrix}c\\t\end{bmatrix}_{q_i}.$$

The generalized Gaussian for integral $c$ denotes its Laurent-polynomial value; for $c=-b<0$ it equals $(-1)^t\begin{bmatrix}b+t-1\\t\end{bmatrix}_{q_i}$.

Fix a simple simply-laced finite root system, its full weight lattice $P$ and coroot lattice $Q^\vee$, with the simply connected root datum $X=P$, $Y=Q^\vee$ and $d_i=1$. Let $\zeta\in\mathbb C^\times$ satisfy $\operatorname{ord}(\zeta^2)=\ell$, where $\ell>h$ is odd and $h$ is the Coxeter number. Both orders $\ell$ and $2\ell$ for $\zeta$ are allowed. Use the full Lusztig form of [[def-root-of-unity-quantum-group-forms]] with this datum, specialized at $q=\zeta$.

Let $\mathcal C_\zeta$ consist of finite-dimensional left modules with a finite $P$-weight decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$ satisfying, for every $h\in Q^\vee$, $i\in I$, $r,t\ge0$ and $c\in\mathbb Z$,

$$K_h|_{M_\mu}=\zeta^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}\operatorname{id},\qquad T_{i,c,t}|_{M_\mu}=\left.\begin{bmatrix}\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c\\t\end{bmatrix}_q\right|_{q=\zeta}\operatorname{id},$$

$$E_i^{(r)}M_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+r\alpha_i},\qquad F_i^{(r)}M_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-r\alpha_i}.$$

The binomial is evaluated as a Laurent polynomial, including negative upper indices, rather than as a ratio of specialized factorials. Morphisms preserve weights and commute with the full algebra. The structure includes all divided powers and toral binomials; ordinary-generator eigenvalue conditions alone are insufficient at a root.

Normalize the symmetric rational bilinear form on $P$ by $(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)=a_{ij}$. Choose a positive integer $D$ with $D(P,P)\subseteq\mathbb Z$ and choose $t\in\mathbb C^\times$ with $t^D=\zeta$. Define the symmetric bicharacter

$$\chi(\lambda,\mu)=t^{D(\lambda,\mu)}.$$

This is part of the choice of braiding. In particular $\chi(\alpha_i,\mu)=\zeta^{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle}$ on the entire selected weight lattice. No coprimality of $\ell$ and the determinant of the Cartan matrix is imposed.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},v)$ be a finite-type symmetrizable Cartan datum, with
$v_i=v^{d_i}$, and let $U_v(\mathfrak g)$ be the scalar extension of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] from $\mathbb Q(v)$ to
$\mathbb C(v)$. The finite-type Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is the Serre Lie
algebra of the matrix $A$
([[def-serre-lie-algebra-of-a-finite-type-cartan-matrix]]). Write
$A_L=\mathbb C[v,v^{-1}]$ and
$A_{DK}=\mathbb C[v,v^{-1},(v_i-v_i^{-1})^{-1}\ (i\in I)]$.

The **Lusztig divided-power form** $U^L_{A_L}(\mathfrak g)$ is the scalar
extension to $A_L$ of the subalgebra $U_A$ defined in
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]. Thus it is generated by the
divided powers $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)}$, the toral elements $K_h^{\pm1}$, and the
toral quantum binomials $T_{i,c,t}$.

The **De Concini–Kac form** $U^{DK}_{A_{DK}}(\mathfrak g)$ is the
$A_{DK}$-subalgebra of $U_v(\mathfrak g)$ generated by $E_i,F_i$ and
$K_h^{\pm1}$. It uses ordinary powers of the root generators. This definition
does not assert that it is free over $A_{DK}$ or that its later specialization
embeds into the Lusztig specialization.

Let $\zeta\in\mathbb C^\times$ be a root of unity. Require
$\zeta_i-\zeta_i^{-1}\ne0$ for each $i$ and put
$\ell_i=\operatorname{ord}(\zeta_i^2)>1$. The specialization map sends
$v\mapsto\zeta$ and has target $\mathbb C$. Define
$$U^{DK}_\zeta(\mathfrak g):=U^{DK}_{A_{DK}}(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{A_{DK},\,v\mapsto\zeta}\mathbb C,\qquad U^L_\zeta(\mathfrak g):=U^L_{A_L}(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{A_L,\,v\mapsto\zeta}\mathbb C.$$
In the standard good odd-order branch, $\zeta$ has odd order $\ell$ and
$\ell$ is relatively prime to every $d_i$; then every $\ell_i=\ell$.

A root-power quotient depends on the chosen toral lattice. In the
convention where the torus is generated by the $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$, define
the **simple-root-power candidate** $u_\zeta^{\mathrm{cand}}(\mathfrak g)$ as the quotient of that ordinary-generator De Concini–Kac algebra by the
two-sided ideal generated by
$E_i^{\ell_i},F_i^{\ell_i},K_i^{\ell_i}-1$ for $i\in I$. This names the quotient construction only. In higher rank it is not the definition of the standard small quantum group: nonsimple positive-root powers need not be killed by imposing only the displayed simple-root powers. No finite dimension, embedding, or higher-rank identification is asserted for this candidate. The rank-one results below use this quotient, where there are no nonsimple positive roots, and denote it by $u_\zeta(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$.

For a standard **small image form**, let $D_\zeta^{(i)}$ be the specialization of the ordinary-generator form with torus generated by the $K_i^{\pm1}$. Define
$$\overline U^L_\zeta=U^L_\zeta/(K_h^\ell-1:h\in P^\vee),\qquad \overline u_\zeta=\operatorname{im}\bigl(D_\zeta^{(i)}\longrightarrow\overline U^L_\zeta\bigr)$$
in the good odd-order branch. The map is the specialization of the generic inclusion into the divided-power form localized by the invertible $v_i-v_i^{-1}$, followed by the toral quotient; it is well defined because those denominators are nonzero at the chosen root. This image definition fixes the actual ordinary-generator form without claiming a presentation by simple root-power relations. The general dimension and root-vector PBW description require separate proofs; no such assertion is implicit here.

The generic inclusion of the ordinary-generator form into the divided-power
form does not by itself assert an inclusion after specializing $v$. The
rank-one items on this page prove a specific root-power quotient and exhibit
the failure of injectivity after specialization. This definition does not
assert a quantum Frobenius theorem or any generic-$v$ semisimplicity at a root
of unity.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: For each root vector the actual integral identity $X_\beta^\ell=[\ell]_\zeta!X_\beta^{(\ell)}=0$ follows from [F1]; its divided root vector exists before specializing. Ordinary monomial spanning therefore truncates every exponent to less than $\ell$. Each remaining ordinary monomial is a nonzero scalar multiple of a distinct specialized divided basis vector, since every $[r]_\zeta!$ with $r<\ell$ is nonzero. They are consequently independent and form the asserted residue bases of the two image halves. This proves both spanning and independence without assuming a presentation of the small algebra.

Every $K_i^L$ is central at the root. By [F2], its central ideal has triangular vector-space form $U^-\otimes\langle K_i^L-1\rangle U^0\otimes U^+$. In the toral quotient the powers $\prod_iK_i^{b_i}$, $0\le b_i<L$, are independent: the formal integral labels have independently varying simple-coroot coordinates, and evaluating a linear relation on these toral characters gives every character of $(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^I$. Multiply by each inverse character and sum; nontrivial character sums vanish by translation and the trivial sum is $L^{|I|}$, so every coefficient is zero. Mixed ordinary reordering uses only $(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{-1}$ and puts all words in negative-torus-positive order. Combining the toral independence with [F2] and step 1.1 proves the stated full triangular basis and dimension. Integral type-1 labels satisfy $K_i^L=1$, so passing to this quotient loses none of the selected module actions.

The symmetries preserve the ordinary form and its inverse before specializing and preserve $U_A$ itself by [F1]. They therefore induce inverse maps on the actual image, rather than merely on an abstract presentation. Their toral images are $K_i^{-1}$ on color $i$ and $K_jK_i$ on a neighbor, so they preserve the ideal generated by $K_j^L-1$. Consequently they are automorphisms of $u$. Applying any such automorphism to the triangular basis gives the asserted transformed basis. A module transported by such a symmetry has its formal labels reflected along with the torus; formal labels are retained even where torus characters coincide.

Choose a negative convex ordering ending in $\alpha_i$. Mixed ordinary reordering shows that $p_i$ has basis $F_i^rK^bE^{\mathbf c}$ with $r<\ell$, $0\le b_j<L$, and all positive residue exponents $\mathbf c$. Indeed other $E_j$ commute with $F_i$ and the repeated-color commutator introduces only a toral element, so these words span; they are part of the basis of step 2.1, hence independent. The full triangular basis is the product of a monomial in the complementary negative root factors and one such $p_i$ basis vector. This is precisely a free right-module decomposition of $u$ over $p_i$. Its inverse antipode preserves $u$ and $p_i$ by the ordinary formulas in [F2], converting it into a free left-module decomposition as well. Applying the algebra automorphisms of step 3.1 proves the transformed parabolic statements. No inference from equality of characters to exact induction has been used.

The ordinary coproduct, counit and antipode preserve the negative Borel $u^-u^0$: $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, $\Delta(K_i)=K_i\otimes K_i$, $S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i$, and $S(K_i)=K_i^{-1}$. The toral relations are Hopf relations, so these descend from [F2]. The Borel is finite by step 2.1, hence is a finite Hopf algebra. Its negative augmentation ideal times the Borel is nilpotent by positive root height and has semisimple finite-torus quotient. These facts are available for the finite-Hopf Frobenius socle argument. General transformed Borels are obtained as algebras, which is all the parabolic induction argument requires. This proves all assertions.
